expect.fees: $10 per person camping fee plus a $6 non-refundable reservation fee (2026 NPS rate); day use is free.
expect.notes: 60% of sites are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
expect.rules: Hard-sided bear canister strongly recommended in this drainage given limited hanging trees and reported aggressive bear activity; parkwide summer fire restrictions (no campfires) are typically in effect by late June; pets and bikes are prohibited beyond the national forest boundary; permit and written itinerary must be carried.
expect.permit: North Cascades National Park backcountry permit required for the overnight stay this peak realistically requires. Reserve via Recreation.gov, watch the mandatory orientation video, then email noca_wilderness@nps.gov up to 3 days before your trip for ranger review and permit issuance, or get a walk-up permit at the Wilderness Information Center (7280 Ranger Station Rd, Marblemount). A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park at the Hannegan Trailhead.
expect.closures: Brush Creek Trail (the final approach corridor toward Whatcom Pass/Indian Mountain) reopened Sept. 2025 after a 3-year closure from the 2022 Brush Creek Fire; Graybeal, Graybeal Stock, and Whatcom Camps remain closed, and the trail is not fully stock-accessible. The Chilliwack River Trail section between the Brush Creek junction and Indian Creek Camp has major fire-related blowdown requiring slow travel. Bear Creek Camp is closed from 2021 fire damage. A bypass has been built around a prior washout at the end of FR 32 to keep the Hannegan Trailhead reachable — check Mt. Baker Ranger District alerts before driving.
expect.landManager: North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness) for the peak and most of the approach; the first several miles from the Hannegan Trailhead to Hannegan Pass cross Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Wilderness).
expect.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
expect.passRequired: Forest Service Recreation Pass for trailhead parking (not the Discover Pass)

expect.name: FS Road 23 (White Chuck River Road)
expect.status: Closed by Forest Order #06-05-25-02 from milepost 3.7 to its terminus at FS Road 27, due to flood damage predating the order's March 19, 2025 effective date — not the later December 2025 Pacific Northwest floods, which occurred after this closure was already in effect. Still closed as of spring 2026 per Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF alerts.
expect.driveNote: From Darrington, follow WA-530 then FS Road 23 south; expect to park at the current MP 3.7 closure point and add roughly 7 miles (14 round trip) of road-walking before reaching the historical trailhead, on top of the ~9-11 mile trail approach to Boulder Basin.
expect.seasonalGate: Even when fully open, the final miles have historically been rough and boulder-strewn, effectively undriveable for most passenger vehicles.

expect.fees: No fee or permit charge to climb or camp — a free self-issue wilderness permit is completed at the trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful interagency pass is required to park at the trailhead.
expect.rules: Standard Glacier Peak Wilderness rules: campfires prohibited above 3,500 ft elevation (effectively all of this route), camp at least 200 ft from water and trails where possible, and pack out all trash.
expect.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead register; no quota or reservation required.
expect.closures: CLOSED: White Chuck Road (FR 23) is closed to vehicles from milepost 3.7 to its end, and Rat Trap Pass Road (FR 27) from milepost 4, for flood damage, with no reopening date. White Chuck River Trail #643 is listed as inaccessible, with no road or trail access, since the 2003 flood. Use the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead and the Pacific Crest Trail instead. Darrington Ranger District: (360) 436-1155.
expect.landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Darrington Ranger District (within the Glacier Peak Wilderness).
